text:
alice: Heads-up — a batch of hosted integration tests are failing on staging CI. Failing across auth + streaming + tool-calling tests. Can someone bisect or rerun? :frowning_face:

ci-bot: Buildkite job #4821 failed: https://ci.redwood.com/builds/4821 (status: failed)
ci-bot: failing tests: test_chat_streaming_auth, test_toolcall_integration, test_schema_validation

alice: Logs (excerpt):
```
ERROR HTTP 401 Unauthorized - token validation failed
stream: upstream timeout after 30.002s
toolcall: schema mismatch: missing "tool_response.result"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/integration/test_toolcall.py", line 72, in test_toolcall_integration
    resp = client.call_tool(payload)
  File "redwood_client.py", line 210, in call_tool
    raise ToolCallError("invalid response")
ToolCallError: invalid response
```

bob: thx. i can kick a rerun first — sometimes infra queues cause 401s if token refreshes race with deployment. i'll rerun jobs that failed.

bob: rerun started (job 4821 -> 4823). pinging @dave for bisect if rerun stays red. :eyes:

carol: fwiw i saw a small auth propagation fix rolled earlier today into main (PR 5592) that touches streaming client header order. could be related. not sure.

dave: i can bisect. what range should i try? latest green on main was 1812200000, first red appears around 1812300000 per commit log. i'll run git bisect between those. need the repro command + env?

alice: repro command: 
```
REDWOOD_API_URL=https://staging.api.redwood.com 
REDWOOD_API_KEY=redacted_for_thread pytest tests/integration/test_chat_streaming.py::test_chat_streaming_auth -q
```

alice: also saw occasional upstream timeouts in the runtime logs, might be unrelated but worth noting.

bob: rerun finished — still failing, same 401 + timeout. so not transient queue. opening bisect now.

infra-bot: Scheduled rerun completed. job 4823 -> status FAILED. Logs archived: https://ci.redwood.com/artifacts/4823/logs.tar.gz

dave: starting bisect now. will report back with first bad commit. if anyone can leave the staging deploy as-is that helps.

carol: leaving deploy in place. also i'll check console for any canary routing changes (rollout config) that might affect token routing.

alice: thanks all. if dave hits the commit that touches auth header ordering, maybe revert for quick hotfix and then re-run the canary slowly. :thumbsup:

dave: first bad commit found: 1812284120 — small change to streaming: reordered header injection to use async hook. reproducing locally now.

bob: nice. can we get a short revert PR to restore previous ordering? i'll draft one and request reviews.

alice: please add an integration-specific test for token propagation edgecases in the PR. otherwise we keep seeing this flip-flop.

dave: agreed. i'll include a test that simulates token refresh during initial stream open.

alice: great. marking this thread resolved for now — follow-up in the PR. :white_check_mark:
